text: Environmental enrichment (EE) is a non-pharmacological intervention that exerts broad effects on both central neural processes and peripheral physiology [ 23 ]. EE involves enhanced housing conditions that provide increased sensory, cognitive, motor, and social stimulation [ 24 ]. In animal models, EE has been demonstrated to promote neurogenesis, facilitate synaptic plasticity, and reduce HPA axis hyperactivity [ 25 , 26 ]. Evidence further indicates that EE influences the microbiota–gut–brain axis. Reported effects include increased microbial diversity, restoration of beneficial taxa such as Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium, augmented short-chain fatty acid production, and improved intestinal barrier integrity, which collectively attenuate stress-induced inflammatory responses [ 27 , 28 ]. These findings suggest that EE modulates interconnected biological pathways disrupted by chronic stress and may serve as a practical approach for addressing both central and peripheral components of stress-related pathology.
source_label: Environmental enrichment attenuates chronic stress–induced disruptions in the gut microbiota, intestinal barrier, and brain
